title: Deprecate and migrate atomic tokens with tooling and rollout plan
creator: Maya Liu
description:
Purpose: Consolidate and deprecate legacy atomic tokens (legacy color ramps, multiple radius tokens, duplicated elevation tokens, and inconsistent type steps) into a single alias + canonical token set. This ticket defines the migration strategy, tooling, rollout phases, and acceptance criteria for the design system and component library.

Background: Over the last 18 months we accumulated divergent tokens as teams optimized for density, charts, and mobile. That drift causes larger bundle sizes, inconsistent visuals across dashboards, and fragile component overrides. Rather than a breaking rename, we will provide aliasing shims, codemods, and runtime warnings to surface usage and shepherd teams to the canonical tokens.

Scope:
- Canonical tokens: color-primary (with semantic aliases), type-scale (6-step responsive scale), radius-atomic (4-step), elevation-micro (5-step).
- Deprecation: Mark 23 legacy tokens deprecated, add alias mapping for backward compat.
- Tooling: Codemod scripts, Figma token file update, Storybook examples, and a consumer migration dashboard.
- Tests: Visual regression snapshots for buttons/tables/charts, automated contrast checks for all semantic colors, and Storybook gating for new token usage.

Non-goals: Removing runtime token feature flags, changing component API surface, or changing component behavior beyond visual tokens (these will be separate follow-ups).

Success criteria:
- All new components authored in the next cycle use canonical tokens (measured by static analysis).
- 90% of flagged legacy token usage either migrated or scheduled (tracked in migration dashboard) within 8 weeks.
- No accessibility regressions (contrast >= WCAG AA for text and >= 3:1 for UI components where applicable).

Deliverables:
- token-alias-map.csv attached to design docs and code repo.
- Codemod: tools/token-migrate (JS) with unit tests.
- Figma file: master tokens updated and team instructions (Drive link).
- Storybook: canonical token story + snapshot tests for Button, Table, Chart components.
- Migration dashboard: small web app listing usages and PR links.

Implementation notes:
- Alias layer: Add short-lived alias tokens that map legacy names to canonical names. At build time emit console warnings when aliases are consumed in production builds for internal apps.
- CSS variables: Publish both --rw-color-primary and deprecated --rw-color-blue-500 until deprecation window closes.
- JS SDK: Provide a lightweight linter plugin for code editors to surface deprecated tokens while editing.
- Codemod strategy: Replace static token imports first, then run a second pass for inline style objects. Keep changes readable and include migration comments.

References and artifacts:
- Confluence migration spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Token+Consolidation+Spec
- Figma tokens file (edit): https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/redwood-tokens/master
- Draft codemod PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/789
- Storybook snapshots branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/compare/storybook/token-snapshots
- Migration dashboard PoC: https://internal.redwood.ai/migration-dashboard (internal)
comments: 2026-03-11 - Internal review: PM (Eleanor Shah) requested we prioritize table/chart contrast regression before wide rollout; added to test plan.
2026-03-12 - Engineering sync: ENG-19840 will land an AST-based token detector; agreed to coordinate codemod output format (file/line + suggested replacement).
2026-03-13 - Design review: Visual QA found button hover elevation token mapping caused a 2px visual shift in dense mode. Decided to add an alias that preserves the visual offset for 1 release cycle.

2026-03-14 - Accessibility review: Ran automatic contrast checker across semantic palette; three semantic token pairs failed AA for small text. Creating follow-up task to adjust semantic foreground tokens.
2026-03-15 - Tooling: Draft codemod PR opened (see PR link). Added instructions for running codemod locally and in CI; next step is adding recovery tests to ensure idempotence.
open_questions: What is the final deprecation window length we communicate to external integrators (8 weeks vs 12 weeks)?
Do we want runtime warnings in production for aliases or only in dev builds?
Should charts get their own extended micro-elevation tokens or rely on the canonical 5-step elevation?
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Visual regressions for dashboards after token swap. Mitigation: Snapshot testing + manual sign-off for top 10 dashboards.
Risk: Internal consumer apps slow to migrate. Mitigation: Provide codemod, editor linter, and migration dashboard showing per-repo usage.
Risk: Accessibility regressions. Mitigation: Run contrast checks in CI and block merge if semantic color fails threshold.
